text:
Evan Bouchard won it for Edmonton in overtime, a power-play snap shot at 3:32 of the extra period with Connor McDavid setting it up. It was the Oilers' third power-play goal of the night, on five chances, and it finished off a game they had led 3-1 before Minnesota came back to tie it.

The score was close to a fair picture of the play. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than just the count, finished at 4.47 for EDM and 4.42 for MIN, and the Oilers deserved to win 51 percent of the time (the share of simulated replays of every shot that they win). Leon Draisaitl scored twice on the power play in the opening 21 minutes, and Mathieu Joseph made it 3-1 in the second. But MIN controlled the rest, out-chancing EDM 1.33 to 0.34 in the third period. Kirill Kaprizov scored at 10:30 and Ryan Hartman tied it at 13:07. Joel Eriksson Ek, who scored the first goal, put eight shots on net. Matt Boldy's best look, a 40 percent chance in the second period, was stopped by Devon Levi, who saved 1.42 more goals than the shots against him should have allowed.

Minnesota went 0 for 3 on the power play and took 10 penalty minutes to Edmonton's six, and the difference decided the game. The facts here carry no streaks or records for either team, so the result stands on its own: EDM took the extra point at home, and MIN left with one of its own for the comeback.
